commentary: Today, DCE iron ore prices trended stronger, with the most-traded contract I2605 closing at 761 yuan, up 1.06% from the previous working day. Spot prices rose 3–5 yuan/mt from the previous day. Traders sold at market prices; steel mills purchased as needed, with inquiry volume moderate. Market trading senƟment was neutral. According to SMM staƟsƟcs, this week's hot metal producƟon aﬀected by blast furnace maintenance was 1.8735 million mt, an increase of 134,600 mt WoW. Due to environmental protecƟon-driven producƟon restricƟons in Hebei, blast furnace operaƟons faced constraints, leading to an overall decline in iron ore demand. Fundamentals remained bearish. AddiƟonally, ports recently began charging corresponding port fees and storage fees to diﬀerent types of cargo owners. This move is expected to raise costs for some imported ore, thereby providing boƩom support for prices of speciﬁc ore varieƟes. Overall, iron ore prices are expected to mainly ﬂuctuate within a range in the short term.
